reasons: [Corporate actions / provider, crypto, VERIFIED] The pinned crypto panel (panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z) records token redenominations and the Terra token swap as genuine price moves, and the harness cannot see them: Market.build detects resets from last_close/previous, but global_panel sets previous = prior close, so ca_ratio is always 1 and crypto runs use ca_mode='adjusted' (nothing scaled, nothing excluded). One-bar ratios beyond x20 through 2023 (read directly from the panel): COCOS 2021-01-23 0.000695->0.9003 (x1,295), DREP 2021-04-02 0.0263->2.828 (x107), SUN 2021-06-18 27.57->0.033 (/834), LUNA 2022-05-12 close 0.00032 then next row 2022-05-31 close 8.87 (old LUNA -> LUNA 2.0, x27,700; LUNC is a separate base from 2022-09-09), BNX 2023-02-22 175.5->1.585 (/111), QUICK 2023-07-21 74.2->0.0597 (/1,243). For E5 these are fake U labels for the 5 sessions before COCOS/DREP/LUNA (discovery fit) and fake D labels before SUN (discovery) and BNX/QUICK (validation 2023), and a long held across BNX or QUICK is scored at about -99% (5,000 USDT notional): one such trade moves a ~600-trade validation average by ~0.17pp and a ~300-trade one by ~0.33pp, enough to decide 'avg net > 0' in a marginal arm, and the D30/directional-ratio diagnostic on crypto counts them as real down-events. E2's crypto run was not hit (its only QUICK trade was 2023-02-20..02-25), but a high-volatility ranker is far more exposed than G2_RET30. The proposal's protocol does not mention unit changes on crypto.

[Look-ahead in the primary fit data, VERIFIED] panel_us-20261008T004105Z and panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z are format panel-global-v1, built with the legacy _finish that deletes a row when the NEXT session's close reverts (manifest qa.spike_rows_dropped 177 US, 2 crypto; the crypto one is LUNA 2022-05-13 inside discovery; the repair manifest's qa_reverting_spike_rows=23 shows 23 US deletions fall inside 2020-01..2023-12). The repo itself classifies this as a future-informed deletion kept 'only as _finish_legacy_v1 for forensic reproduction' and built the causal panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z (causal-close-v2, read_through 2023-12-29). Each deletion removes both label tails (+200% at t-1, -67% at t) and the catastrophic trade entered at open t. The magnitude is tiny (23 of ~3.8M rows) but E5 proposes to fit coefficients, set the 99.5% threshold and run validation A on the legacy panels while a causal panel is on disk, so the primary numbers would carry a documented look-ahead. e1.Study refuses the repair panel's format ('panel-global-v2-units'), so e5.build_dataset cannot route through Study's format check unchanged.

[Provider re-adjustment, US primary run, VERIFIED via ERRATA.md item 1] In the original US panel every price level is in 2026-10 units. A rank-logistic ranker over vol20/dd60/zero20 will concentrate its top 0.5% in sub-$1 names, which are the names that later reverse-split (60% of E2's G2 flags): under the proposal's primary fill A / units=panel their cost tier is too cheap, SKIP_LOT drops names whose adjusted price exceeds the $5,000 notional, and the controls' price_band is the wrong band. ERRATA re-costed E2 from -3.65% to -4.47% from this alone. The proposal relegates as_traded to a sign-only sensitivity; the wrong-way bias sits in the primary.

[Protocol cannot be executed as written, VERIFIED] The crypto fill-B sensitivity is impossible at HEAD with the named panel: execution.execute requires fill B => units='as_traded' (line 383), backtest.run requires a unit_factor column for as_traded (lines 258-261), the crypto panel has no such column, build_us_repair is US-only, and the proposal forbids changes to backtest.py/execution.py. So the crypto pass rule ('sensitivity fill model does not flip the sign') can never be evaluated and no crypto verdict is possible under the protocol's own criteria. E4's crypto protocol (origin/claude/e4-fade-short-side research/E4/protocol.json) used fill A only.

[Survivorship contaminates the rank features and the threshold, US] Unlike one-threshold rules, every E5 feature is a per-session percentile rank over the panel cross-section, which for US is the 2026-10-08 listing snapshot (survivor-only, ~4,800 evaluable names per 2023 session). Ranks of vol20/dd60/etc. at any 2021-2023 session are therefore taken against a cross-section purged of the names that later died (a function of 2026 survival), the D label is under-represented for the feature profiles that precede delisting (inflating logit_U - logit_D exactly where the learner looks), and the frozen 99.5% threshold is calibrated on the purged cross-section and does not transfer to a live cross-section that still contains the future dead. Matched controls (same survivor panel, tercile buckets) absorb part of the label effect but not the within-bucket extreme a squared-rank learner targets. The proposal calls a US-only pass 'weak evidence' yet its FALSIFIER says the null is falsified by an Arm B pass 'in any market': internally inconsistent. Magnitude of the missing cross-section is unknown from the repo (no delisting list).

[Label-generating process changes inside IDX validation (exchange rules, not leakage)] market.REGIMES: ARB 7% from 2020-03-13 to 2023-06-02, 15% from 2023-06-05, symmetric 35/25/20 from 2023-09-04. The whole IDX discovery window (2021-01-22..2022-12-30) is under ARB 7%, where D (-23% within 5 sessions) needs at least four consecutive limit-down closes ((0.93)^3 = -19.6% is insufficient); from 2023-06-05 it needs two sessions and from 2023-09-04 one. COEF_D and the Arm B threshold are thus fitted on a regime where D is mechanically rare and validated on a year whose second half has a different D process; the 'directional ratio' diagnostic on IDX is confounded by this and the protocol does not mention it.

[Window cold-start mismatch between fit and harness, not leakage but a fidelity gap no prior run exposed] backtest.run slices the market to [start, end] before causal_signals (lines 279-287), so inside each harness window the rule's rolling features start cold: vol20 (min 15), dd60 (min 20), med_val shift-1 (min 10), zero20 (20 full), age (= sessions since window start). The fit dataset computes them warm on the full panel. The first ~60 sessions of every discovery and validation run (~25% of 2023) score a feature vector (NaN -> 0.5 rank) the model never saw. F1_ARA and G2_RET30 needed only prev/lock_up, so no recorded run has hit this.

[Minor, IDX fidelity] Market.build applies the special-monitoring-board 10% lock to every one-price bar on all dates although the board exists only from 2023-06-12; in 2021-22 a thin name's single print at +10..34% is treated as ARA-locked, entering E5's `ara` feature and refusing the fill. Inherited by E1-E3; symmetric for rule and controls.

[Checked and sound] Cross-sectional features (medians, ranks) pass the prefix-first check: E2's recorded runs with rel1 report lookahead mode prefix-first-v1, and NaN rows for not-yet-listed names do not change pandas pct ranks. Labels require t+5 inside the period, so no label touches validation from discovery or the holdout from validation; US/crypto windows are sliced before execution so no 2024 row is read (HEAD indeed has no GLOBAL_HOLDOUT; the E4 branch does). Quoted gross-vs-net figures reproduce from trades.csv.gz (-3.67/-4.06, -1.51/-1.90, -3.19/-3.65, -0.10/-0.97). Yahoo volume is split-adjusted (repair/conventions.json, AMZN volume_rel_diff 0), so value, logval20, valr and volr are unit-free (the proposal's 'logval20 not unit-free' is over-cautious). The pinned IDX mirror commit bc0ac7712ce5 is on disk (975/975 manifest files present), so rebuilding panel-20261013T194245Z (sha a924921a, registry 33f81beb bound to it) needs no network; the fallback panel-20261007T225823Z has registry ca_registry-20261007T230210Z bound. E1 vol20 AUC 0.679 verified. The ORACLE arm reads only the label matrix and is not recorded.
